title: Use-case regression suite — durable E2E spine seeded from PROJECT.md primary use cases
description:
Give the project a verification spine that grows with the **product surface**, not with ticket count.

The primary use cases captured at intake (PROJECT.md `primary_use_cases`) seed a small, named E2E suite: one spec per use case under `tests/use-cases/` (in user projects; the seeding hooks into the init wizard / backlog-seeder layer). Tickets touch this suite only when they *change* a use case — never one-spec-per-ticket accretion.

This is what makes the tiered policy (TASK-028) safe: a `uat-only` ticket that skips unit tests is still covered by the use-case suite at release time.

The suite joins the release gate alongside `test:all`. For this repo itself, the use cases are the framework's own top-level flows (init a project, mint a ticket, drive the workflow loop, resume a session, install the plugin) — several already exist as e2e specs and just need to be designated/organized, not rewritten.
acceptance_criteria: A documented convention exists for tests/use-cases/ (one named spec per primary use case) plus an npm run test:use-cases script wired into vitest config
Init/seeding layer generates skeleton use-case specs (marked todo/skipped, not failing) from primary_use_cases answers for fresh projects
CLAUDE.md documents the rule: the suite is part of the release gate and tickets modify it only when a use case changes — suite size tracks product surface, not ticket count
This repo's own primary flows are designated as its use-case suite (reusing existing e2e specs where they already cover the flow)
Full suite green via npm run test:all

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: TIER ASSIGNMENT: verification_tier = tdd — the deliverable includes a generator (skeleton specs from primary_use_cases answers = source logic) and touches vitest config (test infrastructure). GATE: full test:all (test-infra clause). LOCKED DESIGN: (1) Designation-by-manifest — tests/use-cases/USE-CASES.md maps each primary use case to the spec file(s) covering it; existing e2e specs are REFERENCED, never duplicated; a meta-spec validates every referenced path exists. (2) npm run test:use-cases runs tests/use-cases/ via the all-config; the directory is included in test:all automatically. (3) Skeleton generation for user projects: src/use-case-specs.js writes tests/use-cases/<slug>.spec.js with describe + it.todo entries ONLY when the project stack is JS/node; the USE-CASES.md manifest is ALWAYS generated (runner-agnostic). Wired into runInit after seedBacklog; already_initialized skips; idempotent (existing files never clobbered). (4) AC4 self-application: this repo's manifest designates its own primary flows — init/intake, ticket mint, workflow drive (task-store), session resume (lifecycle), plugin install — pointing at the existing e2e specs that cover them.
